identity.title: Imaging the molecular interstellar medium in a gravitationally lensed star-forming galaxy at z = 5.7

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present and study spatially resolved imaging obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) of multiple $^{12}$CO($J=$6$-$5, 8$-$7 and 9$-$8) and two H$_2$O(2$_{02}-$1$_{11}$ and 2$_{11}-$2$_{02}$) emission lines

evidence.quote: The millimeter-bright, gravitationally lensed galaxy SPT0346-52 at $\text{z}=5.6556$ is among the most distant and intrinsically luminous DSFGs known to date.

question.value: What are the intrinsic sizes, kinematics and ISM excitation of the lensed DSFG SPT0346-52 at z=5.66, as traced by mid/high-J CO, H2O and dust continuum in the source plane?

evidence.quote: reconstruct the molecular gas emission in the source plane, (ii) derive their emitting sizes, resolve the gas distribution along the velocity axis and compare with previous observations
as a part of projects 2013.1.00722.S and 2015.1.00117.S during ALMA cycles 2 and 3, respectively (PI: M. Aravena)
as a part of projects 2013.1.00722.S and 2015.1.00117.S during ALMA cycles 2 and 3, respectively (PI: M. Aravena)
Observations of SPT0346-52 were performed with ALMA bands 3 and 4

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: three tunings per band, four SPWs each in FDM, 1.875 GHz per SPW; 7.8125 and 15.625 MHz channels (23 and 31 km/s)

evidence.quote: Each frequency tuning was observed using four spectral windows (SPWs) in Frequency Division Mode (FDM) and a bandwidth of 1.875 GHz per SPW.
Cycle 2 and 3 observations were conducted during April and May of 2015, and during April of 2016, respectively.
(PI: M. Aravena)
its SEPIA band 5 receiver to observe the redshifted emission of the $^{12}$CO $J=10-9$ in SPT0346-52

provided.value: CO(2-1) data from Spilker et al. 2015

evidence.quote: We use previous ATCA observations of the $^{12}$CO $J=$2$-$1 emission line toward SPT0346-52 obtained and described in detail by (cite: spilker15).

what.value: Fixed lens model (SIE plus external shear)

evidence.quote: The lensing mass distribution used was fixed to that obtained by (cite: spilker16) using ALMA 870$\mu$m observations with a resolution of $\sim 0.5''$.

what.value: Herschel SPIRE 250/350/500 um fluxes and ALMA 0.87mm flux used in SED/LVG model

evidence.quote: the ALMA 0.87mm flux (cite: spilker16), and the 250$\mu$m, 350$\mu$m and 500$\mu$m from Herschel/SPIRE observations (cite: ma16)

pipeline_or_manual.value: Independent manual reduction in CASA; no differences from ALMA pipeline calibration

evidence.quote: We performed an independent reduction and calibration of the data, however we did not see differences with respect to the ALMA pipeline calibration.

flux_calibrator.value: quasars and Mars incl. J0411-5149, J0334-401, J0519-4546

evidence.quote: bright quasars and Mars were used for bandpass, flux and phase calibration, including J0411-5149, J0334-401 and J0519-4546.
The visibilities were deconvolved using the `CLEAN` algorithm.
finally used the Briggs weighting with a robustness factor of 0.5

masking.value: tight circular aperture radius 5", clean to 2 sigma

evidence.quote: we masked this source using a tight circular aperture around it with a radius of $5''$, cleaning down to $2\sigma$

continuum_subtraction.value: power law fit to extracted spectra

evidence.quote: We subtracted the continuum emission from the line profiles by fitting a power law to the extracted spectra.
We created data cubes at different channel resolutions, averaging by 2, 4 and 8 original channels.

what.value: Lens model parameters and visibility-domain method

evidence.quote: The method relies on modeling the visibilities instead of images and simultaneously determining self-calibration phases (cite: hezaveh13).
using the method described in (cite: weiss07). This method is based on a spherical, multi-component, large velocity gradient (LVG) model.

unstated_but_needed: Line-free channels and continuum fit ranges
Lens-fit sampler, priors and likelihood details in visibility fitting
LVG fit priors and fitting procedure

method.value: CLEAN with Briggs 0.5; 7" aperture photometry on 4-channel-averaged cubes; Gaussian fits for FWHM; direct integration for fluxes

evidence.quote: The line FWHM and central frequency are computed from single, one-dimensional Gaussian fits to the emission line profiles.

method.value: Visibility-domain lens modelling with circular Gaussian source (4 free params), fixed SIE+shear lens, nine velocity bins of 100 km/s

evidence.quote: The emission regions have been assumed to have a circularly symmetric Gaussian light profile with four free parameters: flux density F$_S$, scale radius R$_S$, and position offsets

key_parameters.value: bins from -400 to 400 km/s; outer bins widened by 4x

evidence.quote: Each of the lens-modeled lines in SPT0346-52 are split into nine velocity bins with a width of 100 km s$^{-1}$, ranging from $-400$ to $400$ km s$^{-1}$.
we also performed a reconstruction of each line using a single, wide velocity channel (from $- 2\sigma_{vel}$ to $2\sigma_{vel}$) as a benchmark for comparison.

method.value: Compare observed and intrinsic (delensed) CO J/CO(2-1) intensity ratios and magnification per velocity bin

evidence.quote: we explore the variation of the magnification and CO line ratios as a function of velocity (i.e. along the line of sight).
This behaviour is broadly consistent with the results presented by (cite: dong18)

method.value: Spherical multi-component LVG model fit to intrinsic CO and continuum fluxes

evidence.quote: This method is based on a spherical, multi-component, large velocity gradient (LVG) model.
we assume a fixed CO line width, corresponding to the weighted average line width value (642 km s$^{-1}$).

assumptions.value: CO(2-1)/CO(1-0) brightness ratio R21=0.9 for SLED comparison

evidence.quote: assuming a brightness temperature line ratio $R_{21}=T^B_{21}/T^B_{10}=0.9$ (cite: carilli&walter13)

validation.value: Gas mass compared with dynamical mass

evidence.quote: even higher than the dynamical mass estimate of $1.5\times10^{11}\ M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ obtained from the high resolution CO($2-1$) imaging (cite: spilker15)
The data were reduced and imaged using the Common Astronomy Software Application package `CASA`
Offline data calibration and flagging was performed using the `CLASS` software package
Using the `VISILENS` code and lens model parameters obtained in (cite: spilker16) we reconstructed the lensed galaxy in the source-plane
the single Gaussian fit yields an integrated flux of $\sim 17.3 \pm 2.9$ Jy km s$^{-1}$
$T_{\text{kin}}$     | $43   \pm 14$ K

findings_qualitative.value: Higher-J CO traces more compact regions; CO sizes larger than dust continuum sizes

evidence.quote: The CO sizes show a clear trend of decreasing size with increasing $J$

claims.hypothesis: Do higher-J CO lines trace more compact regions?
Is the kinematics a merger or a disk?
claims.result: gradients suggest disk-like structure in some lines, size variations in CO(2-1) and H2O 2_11-2_02

evidence.quote: This could be attributed to a compact merger or turbulent disk rotation.

claims.experiment: LVG modelling of the CO SLED
claims.result: Tkin ~43 K, log n ~4.9, SLED peaks near J=8-7
claims.finding: Dense warm gas, similar to quasar hosts; model not fully constrained

evidence.quote: Modeling of the ISM in SPT0346-52 based on delensed fluxes indicate a highly dense and warm medium

why_this_method.value: Gaussian profile chosen to minimize free source parameters

evidence.quote: the choice of a Gaussian profile compared to e.g. Sérsic or other commonly used source profiles is justified in order to minimize the number of free source parameters.

limitations_admitted.value: LVG model not fully constrained because the CO SLED peak is not traced

evidence.quote: our inability to trace the peak of the CO SLED with our current observations and thus our radiative transfer model is not fully constrained

referee_caveats_inferred: Single Gaussian source model may bias sizes and magnifications
LVG gas mass exceeds dynamical mass

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~50-100 GB for the six ALMA tunings
reproducibility.score_reason: Data are archival projects with named method, but lens-fit and LVG details are largely deferred to earlier papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Key analysis depends on VISILENS and inherited lens model and LVG code with incomplete settings.

companion_papers.why: CO(8-7) reconstruction of the same source
